newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian Chinese man jailed for riot - paper.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian Chinese man jailed for riot - paper.

text.p: An Indonesian man of Chinese descent has been jailed for inciting a riot in West Java in January during which churches and Chinese temples were attacked, Kompas newspaper reported on Tuesday.

The newspaper said Tjio Kim Tjoan, 55, was sentenced on Monday to three years and six months in jail after being found guilty of provoking the riot in Rengasdengklok, 50 km (30 miles) east of Jakarta.
Court officials could not be reached for comment.
The newspaper quoted judges as saying Tjio had scolded Moslem youths who were beating drums to summon people to eat before the start of daytime fasting during the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
A mainly Moslem mob later attacked churches and Chinese temples and looted homes and shops. Sixteen cars were also burned.
At least 20 people were arrested after the violence, but there was no word on whether they were still in custody or were to face charges.
Elsewhere, 30 people were brought to court for involvement in a riot late last month in Pekalongan, Central Java, that also targeted ethnic Chinese.
At least 60 shops were burned or ransacked, two cars were set ablaze and a state-run bank was damaged during the violence, in which about 1,000 people attacked the property of mainly ethnic Chinese.
The riot was apparently sparked by reports that a popular singer who used to be a supporter of the Moslem-based United Development Party (PPP) had switched allegiance to the ruling Golkar party.
Indonesia has been rocked by a series of ethnic and religious riots since late last year.
